1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
18: 
19: ## Mobile browser games
20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
24: - Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D open-world game set in Rio de Janeiro, based on the user’s Portuguese description.

## Requirements
- Open world with character choices, varied weapons, cars to steal, and police patrols in motorcycles and cars.
- Start with R$ 250 and a tuned motorcycle; earn money through delivery, taxi, or car dismantling jobs.
- Require motorcycle and car driving licenses; show a minimap at the upper right.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finishing.
- For visual checks, save a small JPEG (viewport ≤1280px) and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Built a browser-based Three.js game with Portuguese UI and keyboard/touch controls.
- Implemented simplified license exams as travel-to-autoescola and interact; included four selectable weapon states.
- Used procedural city geometry and placeholder-style vehicles/characters; no external game assets.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created `index.html`, `style.css`, and `game.js` implementing the game UI and gameplay systems.
- Added open-world city grid, beach, hills, landmarks, pedestrians, traffic, police patrols, motorcycle, and cars.
- Added character selection, jobs menu, delivery/taxi/license/chop jobs, money and wanted level, vehicle entry/exit, minimap, and responsive touch controls.
- `node --check game.js` passed.
- Opened the game in Playwright and saved/inspected `screenshots/latest.jpg`.

### Active
- Validate gameplay in browser and fix any issues discovered.
- Browser reported a missing `/favicon.ico` (404); no other browser runtime error was reported.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect the browser gameplay, particularly job flow, interactions, vehicle entry, and the license progression.
2. Fix any runtime or gameplay defects; optionally add a favicon to clear the 404.
3. Re-run checks and capture a fresh JPEG if visual changes are made.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game UI, menus, HUD, character selection, job options.
- `style.css`: Game presentation and responsive/mobile styling.
- `game.js`: Three.js scene, controls, vehicles, police, missions, minimap, and game state.
- `screenshots/latest.jpg`: Most recent visual check.

## Important Context
- Local preview was started with `python3 -m http.server 3002`; Playwright opened `http://localhost:3002`.
- Changes are not committed.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D open-world game set in Rio de Janeiro.

## Requirements
- Open-world exploration, customizable character, varied weapons, stealable cars, and police patrols in motorcycles and cars.
- Start with R$ 250 and a tuned motorcycle; earn money through delivery, taxi, or car dismantling jobs.
- Require motorcycle and car licenses; show a minimap at the upper right.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them when finishing.
- For visual checks, save a small JPEG (viewport ≤1280px) and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Implemented a browser-based Three.js game with Portuguese UI, keyboard and touch controls, and procedural city geometry.
- License exams are represented by reaching the autoescola and interacting; weapon states cycle through four options.
- Used procedural placeholder vehicles and characters; no external game assets.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the game UI and gameplay systems in `index.html`, `style.css`, and `game.js`.
- Added city scenery, landmarks, beach, pedestrians, traffic, police patrols, motorcycle, and cars.
- Added character selection, jobs, money and wanted level, vehicle entry/exit, licenses, minimap, and responsive touch controls.
- `node --check game.js` passed.
- Opened the game in Playwright and inspected `screenshots/latest.jpg` at 1280×800.

### Active
- Validate gameplay flows in-browser, including jobs, interactions, vehicle entry, and license progression.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Test the job and license flows, vehicle interactions, and police behavior in the browser; fix any defects found.
2. Optionally add a favicon to clear the browser’s `/favicon.ico` 404.
3. Re-run checks and capture a fresh JPEG if visual changes are made.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game UI, menus, HUD, character selection, and job options.
- `style.css`: Game presentation and responsive/mobile styling.
- `game.js`: Three.js scene, controls, vehicles, police, missions, minimap, and game state.
- `screenshots/latest.jpg`: Most recent visual check.

## Important Context
- Browser load showed a missing `/favicon.ico` (404); no other browser runtime error was reported.
- Changes are uncommitted.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D open-world game set in Rio de Janeiro.

## Requirements
- Include open-world exploration, customizable character, varied weapons, stealable cars, police patrols in motorcycles and cars, jobs, licenses, and an upper-right minimap.
- Start with R$ 250 and a tuned motorcycle; offer delivery, taxi, and car dismantling jobs.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them when finishing.
- For visual checks, save a JPEG viewport no larger than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Built a browser-based Three.js game with Portuguese UI, keyboard and touch controls, and procedural city geometry.
- License exams are completed by reaching the autoescola and interacting; weapons cycle through four options.
- Used procedural placeholder vehicles and characters; no external game assets.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented game UI, city scenery, landmarks, beach, pedestrians, traffic, police patrols, motorcycle, and cars in `index.html`, `style.css`, and `game.js`.
- Added character selection, jobs, money and wanted level, vehicle entry/exit, licenses, minimap, and responsive touch controls.
- `node --check game.js` passed.
- Fixed malformed CSS in `style.css` that prevented the stylesheet from parsing and left UI controls behind the game canvas.
- Added an inline SVG favicon in `index.html`.
- Confirmed the stylesheet now parses, the welcome overlay is above the canvas, and the UI is interactive in the browser.

### Active
- Validate gameplay flows in-browser, including jobs, interactions, vehicle entry, license progression, and police behavior.
- Capture and inspect a fresh screenshot after the CSS fix.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue browser testing of jobs, vehicle interactions, licenses, and police behavior; fix defects found.
2. Capture and inspect the latest JPEG at a viewport no larger than 1280px.
3. Re-run checks and report completion, briefly noting assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game UI, menus, HUD, character selection, job options, and inline favicon.
- `style.css`: Game presentation and responsive/mobile styling; recently fixed malformed gradient.
- `game.js`: Three.js scene, controls, vehicles, police, missions, minimap, and game state.
- `screenshots/latest.jpg`: Previous visual check, predating the CSS fix.

## Important Context
- The game is served at `http://localhost:3002/`.
- Earlier screenshot was `screenshots/latest.jpg` at 1280×800; refresh it after the recent visual fix.
- Browser previously reported only a missing `/favicon.ico` and WebGL readback performance warnings; the favicon has since been added.
- Changes are uncommitted.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D open-world game set in Rio de Janeiro.

## Requirements
- Include open-world exploration, a customizable character, varied weapons, stealable cars, police patrols in motorcycles and cars, jobs, licenses, and an upper-right minimap.
- Start with R$ 250 and a tuned motorcycle; offer delivery, taxi, and car dismantling jobs.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them when finishing.
- For visual checks, save a JPEG viewport no larger than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Built a browser-based Three.js game with Portuguese UI, keyboard and touch controls, and procedural city geometry.
- License exams are completed by reaching the autoescola and interacting; weapons cycle through four options.
- Used procedural placeholder vehicles and characters; no external game assets.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented game UI, city scenery, landmarks, beach, pedestrians, traffic, police patrols, motorcycle, and cars in `index.html`, `style.css`, and `game.js`.
- Added character selection, jobs, money and wanted level, vehicle entry/exit, licenses, minimap, and responsive touch controls.
- Fixed malformed CSS in `style.css` that prevented the stylesheet from parsing and left UI controls behind the game canvas.
- Added an inline SVG favicon in `index.html`.
- Confirmed the welcome overlay renders above the canvas and is interactive.
- Started the game in-browser, opened the jobs menu, accepted delivery, entered the motorcycle, cycled to the pistol, fired (wanted level increased), and canceled the delivery job.
- `node --check game.js` passed.

### Active
- Validate job completion, vehicle interactions, license progression, and police behavior in-browser.
- Capture and inspect a fresh JPEG screenshot after the CSS fix.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue browser testing of jobs, vehicle interactions, licenses, and police behavior; fix defects found.
2. Capture and inspect the latest JPEG at a viewport no larger than 1280px.
3. Re-run checks and report completion, briefly noting assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game UI, menus, HUD, character selection, job options, and inline favicon.
- `style.css`: Game presentation and responsive/mobile styling; malformed gradient was fixed.
- `game.js`: Three.js scene, controls, vehicles, police, missions, minimap, and game state.
- `screenshots/latest.jpg`: Previous visual check, predating the CSS fix.

## Important Context
- The game is served at `http://localhost:3002/`.
- Browser testing is currently in the active game; the delivery job was canceled after acceptance.
- `git status --short` showed project files as untracked, including `game.js`, `index.html`, and `style.css`; changes are uncommitted.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D open-world game set in Rio de Janeiro.

## Requirements
- Include open-world exploration, a customizable character, varied weapons, stealable cars, police patrols in motorcycles and cars, jobs, licenses, and an upper-right minimap.
- Start with R$ 250 and a tuned motorcycle; offer delivery, taxi, and car dismantling jobs.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them when finishing.

## Decisions
- Built a browser-based Three.js game with Portuguese UI, keyboard and touch controls, and procedural city geometry.
- License exams are completed by reaching the autoescola and interacting; weapons cycle through four options.
- Used procedural placeholder vehicles and characters; no external game assets.

## Work State
### Completed

2. Run final checks and report completion, briefly noting assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game UI, menus, HUD, character selection, job options, and inline favicon.
- `style.css`: Game presentation and responsive/mobile styling.
- `game.js`: Three.js scene, controls, vehicles, police, missions, minimap, and game state.
- `screenshots/latest.jpg`: Latest inspected viewport screenshot.

## Important Context

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D open-world game set in Rio de Janeiro.

## Requirements
- Include open-world exploration, a customizable character, varied weapons, stealable cars, police patrols in motorcycles and cars, jobs, licenses, and an upper-right minimap.

## Decisions
- Built a browser-based Three.js game with Portuguese UI, keyboard and touch controls, and procedural city geometry.
- License exams are completed by reaching the autoescola and interacting; weapons cycle through four options.
- Used procedural placeholder vehicles and characters; no external game assets.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented game UI, city scenery, landmarks, beach, pedestrians, traffic, police patrols, motorcycle, and cars in `index.html`, `style.css`, and `game.js`.

- `index.html`: Game UI, menus, HUD, character selection, job options, and inline favicon.
- `style.css`: Game presentation and responsive/mobile styling.
- `game.js`: Three.js scene, controls, vehicles, police, missions, minimap, and game state.
- `screenshots/latest.jpg`: Latest inspected viewport screenshot.

playwright-cli - run playwright mcp commands from terminal

Usage: playwright-cli <command> [args] [options]
Usage: playwright-cli -s=<session> <command> [args] [options]

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser
  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element
  click <target> [button]     perform click on a web page
  dblclick <target> [button]  perform double click on a web page
  fill <target> <text>        fill text into editable element
  drag <startTarget> <endTarget> perform drag and drop between two elements
  drop <target>               drop files or data onto an element
  hover <target>              hover over element on page
  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown
  upload <files...>           upload one or multiple files
  check <target>              check a checkbox or radio button
  uncheck <target>            uncheck a checkbox or radio button
  snapshot [target]           capture page snapshot to obtain element ref
  find [text]                 search the page snapshot for text or a regexp, returning matching nodes with surrounding context (like search snippets)
  eval <func> [target]        evaluate javascript expression on page or element
  dialog-accept [prompt]      accept a dialog
  dialog-dismiss              dismiss a dialog
  resize <w> <h>              resize the browser window
  delete-data                 delete session data

Navigation:
  go-back                     go back to the previous page
  go-forward                  go forward to the next page
  reload                      reload the current page

Keyboard:
  press <key>                 press a key on the keyboard, `a`, `arrowleft`
  keydown <key>               press a key down on the keyboard
  keyup <key>                 press a key up on the keyboard

Mouse:
  mousemove <x> <y>           move mouse to a given position
  mousedown [button]          press mouse down
  mouseup [button]            press mouse up
  mousewheel <dx> <dy>        scroll mouse wheel

Save as:
  screenshot [target]         screenshot of the current page or element
  pdf                         save page as pdf

Tabs:
  tab-list                    list all tabs
  tab-new [url]               create a new tab
  tab-close [index]           close a browser tab
  tab-select <index>          select a browser tab

Storage:
  state-load <filename>       loads browser storage (authentication) state from a file
  state-save [filename]       saves the current storage (authentication) state to a file
  cookie-list                 list all cookies (optionally filtered by domain/path)
  cookie-get <name>           get a specific cookie by name
  cookie-set <name> <value>   set a cookie with optional flags
  cookie-delete <name>        delete a specific cookie

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D open-world game set in Rio de Janeiro.

## Requirements
- Include open-world exploration, a customizable character, varied weapons, stealable cars, police patrols in motorcycles and cars, jobs, licenses, and an upper-right minimap.
- Start with R$ 250 and a tuned motorcycle; include delivery, taxi, and car dismantling jobs.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them when finishing.
- For visual checks, save a JPEG viewport no larger than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Implemented a browser-based Three.js game with Portuguese UI, keyboard and touch controls, and procedural city geometry.
- License exams are completed by reaching the autoescola and interacting; weapons cycle through four options.
- Used procedural placeholder vehicles and characters; no external game assets.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented game UI, city scenery, landmarks, beach, pedestrians, traffic, police patrols, motorcycle, and cars in `index.html`, `style.css`, and `game.js`.
- Added character selection, jobs, money and wanted level, vehicle entry/exit, licenses, minimap, and responsive touch controls.
- Fixed malformed CSS and added an inline SVG favicon.
- Updated car dismantling to allow entering the marked sedan without CNH B; entering starts the delivery leg, and interacting at the scrapyard completes it.
- Improved wanted-level timer handling to reset on new crimes and follow the active vehicle.
- Browser-tested game start, jobs menu, accepting/canceling delivery, vehicle entry/exit, weapon selection/firing, and movement.
- Verified delivery job progressed from pickup to destination.
- `node --check game.js` passed.
- Captured and inspected `screenshots/latest.jpg` at 1280×800.

### Active
- (none)

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue browser testing car dismantling, license progression, police behavior, and job completion if further verification is needed.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game UI, menus, HUD, character selection, jobs, and favicon.
- `style.css`: Game presentation and responsive/mobile styling.
- `game.js`: Three.js scene, controls, vehicles, police, missions, minimap, and game state.
- `screenshots/latest.jpg`: Latest inspected 1280×800 viewport.

## Important Context
- Game is served at `http://localhost:3002/`.
- Project files are uncommitted and appear untracked in `git status --short`, including `game.js`, `index.html`, and `style.css`.
- Assumptions: city and vehicles use procedural placeholder graphics; license exams are completed through interaction at the driving school.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D open-world game set in Rio de Janeiro.
- Improve realism with a running, animated character who starts with a 30-round Glock and can earn money.

## Requirements
- Include open-world exploration, a customizable character, varied weapons, stealable cars, police patrols in motorcycles and cars, jobs, licenses, and an upper-right minimap.
- Start with R$ 250 and a tuned motorcycle; include delivery, taxi, and car dismantling jobs.
- Character should run and perform movements; start with a Glock holding 30 shots to earn money.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them when finishing.
- For visual checks, save a JPEG viewport no larger than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Implemented a browser-based Three.js game with Portuguese UI, keyboard and touch controls, and procedural city geometry.
- License exams are completed by reaching the autoescola and interacting; weapons cycle through four options.
- Used procedural placeholder vehicles and characters; no external game assets.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented game UI, city scenery, landmarks, beach, pedestrians, traffic, police patrols, motorcycle, and cars in `index.html`, `style.css`, and `game.js`.
- Added character selection, jobs, money and wanted level, vehicle entry/exit, licenses, minimap, and responsive touch controls.
- Fixed malformed CSS and added an inline SVG favicon.
- Updated car dismantling to allow entering the marked sedan without CNH B; entering starts the delivery leg, and interacting at the scrapyard completes it.
- Improved wanted-level timer handling to reset on new crimes and follow the active vehicle.
- Browser-tested game start, jobs menu, accepting/canceling delivery, vehicle entry/exit, weapon selection/firing, and movement.
- Verified delivery job progressed from pickup to destination; `node --check game.js` passed.
- Captured and inspected `screenshots/latest.jpg` at 1280×800.

### Active
- Implement the newer request for a more realistic running character with movement animations and a starting Glock with 30 rounds, supporting money-earning gameplay.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect weapon, player movement, and money/job logic in `game.js` and related UI in `index.html`.
2. Add character running/movement animation and implement the requested 30-round starting Glock and suitable money-earning gameplay.
3. Test the changes in-browser and inspect only the newest screenshot at no more than 1280px.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game UI, menus, HUD, character selection, jobs, and favicon.
- `style.css`: Game presentation and responsive/mobile styling.
- `game.js`: Three.js scene, controls, vehicles, police, missions, weapons, and game state.
- `screenshots/latest.jpg`: Latest inspected 1280×800 viewport.

## Important Context
- Game is served at `http://localhost:3002/`.
- Project changes are uncommitted; `game.js`, `index.html`, and `style.css` were reported as untracked.
- Current `makePerson()` builds a static figure; weapon names are `DESARMADO`, `PISTOLA`, `ESCOPETA`, and `SMG`; `selectedWeapon` is initialized to `0`.
- Assumptions: city and vehicles use procedural placeholder graphics; license exams are completed through interaction at the driving school.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D open-world game set in Rio de Janeiro.
- Improve realism with an animated running character and a starting Glock with 30 rounds, while supporting money-earning gameplay.

## Requirements
- Include open-world exploration, a customizable character, varied weapons, stealable cars, police patrols in motorcycles and cars, jobs, licenses, and an upper-right minimap.
- Start with R$ 250 and a tuned motorcycle; include delivery, taxi, and car dismantling jobs.
- Character should run and perform movements; start with a Glock holding 30 shots.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them when finishing.
- For visual checks, save a JPEG viewport no larger than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Implemented a browser-based Three.js game with Portuguese UI, keyboard and touch controls, and procedural city geometry.
- License exams are completed by reaching the autoescola and interacting; weapons cycle through four options.
- Used procedural placeholder vehicles, characters, and targets; no external game assets.
- Added fictional cash targets as an optional way to earn money with the Glock; firing alerts police.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented game UI, city scenery, landmarks, beach, pedestrians, traffic, police patrols, motorcycle, and cars in `index.html`, `style.css`, and `game.js`.
- Added character selection, jobs, money and wanted level, vehicle entry/exit, licenses, minimap, and responsive touch controls.
- Fixed malformed CSS and added an inline SVG favicon.
- Updated car dismantling to allow entering the marked sedan without CNH B; entering starts the delivery leg, and interacting at the scrapyard completes it.
- Improved wanted-level timer handling to reset on new crimes and follow the active vehicle.
- Added articulated player limbs, walk/run animation, visible Glock model, 30-round starting ammo, ammo HUD, and a mobile fire button.
- Added fictional cash targets that award R$ 100 when hit.
- Verified `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check` pass.
- Browser-tested start and firing: game starts, HUD reads `GLOCK 17`, and ammo decrements from `30 / 30` to `29 / 30`.
- Captured and inspected the latest viewport JPEG at `screenshots/latest.jpg` (1280×800).

### Active
- (none)

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. If further polishing is requested, continue from the current uncommitted changes and verify any new gameplay or visual adjustments in-browser.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game UI, menus, HUD, mobile controls, and favicon.
- `style.css`: Game presentation and responsive/mobile styling.
- `game.js`: Three.js scene, character animation, controls, vehicles, police, missions, weapons, and game state.
- `screenshots/latest.jpg`: Latest inspected 1280×800 viewport.

## Important Context
- Game is served at `http://localhost:3002/`.
- Project changes are uncommitted; `game.js`, `index.html`, and `style.css` are modified.
- Character, city, vehicles, and targets use procedural placeholder graphics.
- Assumption: fictional cash targets provide a simple optional money-earning activity; firing raises wanted level.

The Rio de Janeiro game is implemented in `index.html`, `style.css`, and `game.js`. It includes the requested exploration, jobs, vehicles, police, licenses, minimap, character animation, and starting Glock with 30 rounds. I verified the game starts and firing reduces the ammo count, and saved the latest 1280×800 screenshot to `screenshots/latest.jpg`.

Assumption: the optional fictional cash targets provide a simple way to earn money; firing alerts police.
